Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood CSM); Alex Morgan (CTO), Sana Rahman (SRE), Miguel Torres (Product), Rina Patel (Procurement)
Shared links: onboarding runbook: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding-runbook, security pack: https://redwood.example.com/security/lighthouse (note: links are placeholders)

Summary (auto): Quick intake to align scope for a 4-week pilot, confirm security constraints for private/VPC deployment, agree on success metrics (p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens), and schedule technical deep-dive for benchmarking.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about an hour, I'm Jordan, I run the AE for this account. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Alex (Customer): Alex here, hey.
[00:15] Sana (Customer): Sana - SRE.
[00:18] Miguel (Customer): Miguel product.
[00:21] Rina (Customer): Rina from procurement.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood): Priya here, hi all, I'll be the solutions eng on the pilot.
[00:28] Marcus (Redwood): Marcus, CSM, I'll handle cadence and onboarding ops.
[00:32] Jordan: Cool, thanks. The goal today is a fast intake — scope the pilot, identify blockers (security/networking), and agree next steps.

[02:05] Alex: High level — we're building an internal assistant for customer success and docs search, primary constraint is that any api calls must not route outside our VPC or must be approved for data residency. We also need SOC2 logs and an audit trail.

[02:38] Priya: Understood. For VPC we have two options: Redwood Private (we can do a VPC peering or private link) or Dedicated hosted with egress controls. We should confirm if you need air-gapped on-prem later.

[03:15] Sana: Air-gap not initially, but data residency in our US-EAST region and KMS integration is required. We use AWS KMS and want HSM-backed keys.

[03:50] Jordan: Perfect. We'll capture that. Marcus — can you note the KMS requirement?
[03:55] Marcus: Noted. Also we'll attach our KMS integration guide after the call.

[05:10] Miguel: For success metrics, product wants to see p95 under 800ms for short prompts and cost below $X per 1k tokens, but we'll confirm the absolute numbers. Also we need model quality checks — hallucination rate tolerances.

[05:45] Priya: For the pilot we recommend starting with our verified Llama-variant (note: transcript may show Llama-very or Lama 2), or a Redwood-curated open model. We can run an A/B against a smaller model to measure tradeoffs. We'll provide eval harness.

[06:30] Alex: How about caching? If we cache prefixes or use KV cache, we can reduce cost. Is that supported in Private deployments?

[06:49] Priya: Yes, KV cache and prefix caching supported; in Private mode it's configurable. Small caveat — cache warm-up can affect early latency numbers, we'll include warm-up runs in the bench plan.

[08:10] Jordan: Let's talk timeline. Customer wants a 4-week pilot then a go/no-go. Week 0 is setup, week 1 bench and smoke, week 2 integrations, weeks 3–4 iteration and handoff. Is that realistic?

[08:32] Alex: Sounds right, we have a target internal review in week 5.

[09:05] Rina (Procurement): On procurement — we need vendor SOC2 and ISO docs plus an outline of standard contract terms. If Dedicated is chosen we may negotiate longer term commit; otherwise we'll do a month-to-month pilot.

[09:48] Jordan: We'll send the SOC2 pack and our standard MSA. Note: some of the doc links in the transcript may show as Redwood Sec Pack.

[11:12] Priya: Technical blockers we should surface: network egress, SSO/SAML for admin, KMS for key management, and data retention policy. Also, which telemetry do you need? Token-level billing, traces?

[11:40] Sana: Token-level breakdown and per-route latency charts are helpful. We also want tracing hooks to tie requests back to user IDs for audit — if that's possible without PII leaking.

[12:05] Priya: We support token-level cost breakdown in the console and tracing hooks — we'll share sample trace logs. We'll discuss redaction/PII filters in the sec deep-dive.

[13:30] Alex: One question — if we do Private deployment to our VPC, do requests ever egress to Redwood hosted models? We want guarantees.

[13:52] Jordan: In Private mode, computation stays in your network. For Hosted we do route to Redwood infra. We also have fallback policies — if dedicated capacity runs out we can failover to a compatible hosted variant but that is configurable (we'll ensure it's off for this pilot unless you want it).

[14:40] Miguel: How are rollouts handled? We want canary and ability to pin versions of models for a route.

[15:02] Priya: We have rollouts and pinning per route — canary percent, A/B, automatic fallback. We'll include docs and a demo in the tech deep-dive.

[16:30] Alex: On observability, we need retention of logs for 365 days for audit. Is that an add-on?

[16:48] Jordan: Retention beyond default is add-on; we can include options and cost in the pricing sheet.

[18:10] Rina: On pricing — will you show dedicated capacity per GPU-hour or per-request?

[18:25] Jordan: Dedicated is committed capacity (monthly/annual) with a predictable unit cost; Hosted is usage-based per token. We'll send a comparative pricing sheet with examples based on your traffic profile.

[19:05] Alex: We'll share a sample traffic CSV. Any preferred format?

[19:14] Priya: CSV with timestamp, route, prompt length, response length. That helps us model batching and cost.

[20:05] Marcus: I'll set up a shared Google folder and put the runbook and template, plus a short checklist for the pilot.

[22:00] Priya: Technical deep-dive — we propose Wednesday next week, 90 minutes. We'll run through provisioning, a live bench with your sample traffic (or synthetic if you prefer), and a VPC peering walkthrough.

[22:30] Alex: Wednesday works for us. We'll confirm attendees from infra.

[24:10] Miguel: A few nitty-gritty items: auth flow from our app to the Redwood route, expected tokenization differences across models, and evaluation harness to check hallucination.

[24:36] Priya: We'll include a note about tokenization variance — different tokenizers mean different token counts; it's important for cost modeling. We'll also share an eval harness for automated tests.

[26:50] Alex: For compliance we require SSO (SAML) and RBAC for admin console.

[27:05] Jordan: We support SAML SSO and granular RBAC — we'll share the SSO integration guide.

[28:30] Sana: Network specifics — we are likely to prefer VPC peering over a public endpoint. Can you run through the peering prerequisites?

[28:47] Priya: Sure — you'll need a VPC with private subnets, a role for cross-account peering, route tables updated, and we'll provide a terraform snippet. Note: some customers use AWS PrivateLink instead.

[30:15] Alex: If we start with hosted for speed and then flip to private, what is the migration effort?

[30:30] Priya: Migration is relatively straightforward — model pinning helps. You may need to reconfigure endpoints and update DNS or peering; we'll provide a migration checklist. Expect 1–3 days of work for a basic route.

[32:05] Miguel: Bench specifics — what's included in your benchmark? p50/p95 latency, throughput, token throughput, and failure/retry rates?

[32:25] Priya: Yes to all those. We'll also measure cold-starts and KV-cache hit rates. We'll run warm-up and steady-state tests.

[34:00] Jordan: A few risks to call out: initial cold cache affecting latency numbers, network egress causing security questions, and early-stage hallucination checks. We should document mitigations.

[35:42] Alex: On the hallucination metric — how do you recommend measuring? We'll probably use a QA set and measure precision/recall on factuality.

[36:05] Priya: We'll give an eval harness template. Many customers use a human-in-the-loop threshold initially.

[38:10] Rina: Contract timeline — if pilot shows promise we'll fast-track procurement, but we need standard terms. Also, can you share cybersecurity questionnaires?

[38:35] Marcus: We'll send the vendor security packet and if needed a SOC2 attestation.

[40:20] Priya: One more technical note — batching helps cost but can increase tail latency. For interactive assistant workflows you may want a smaller batch target or latency-first config. For high-throughput async jobs you can batch more aggressively.

[41:05] Alex: That answers the latency vs cost tradeoff. We'll map out 2 routes: interactive support and nightly summarization batch jobs.

[43:00] Miguel: For the nightly job, can we use quantized models to cut cost?

[43:18] Priya: Yes — we can recommend quantization profiles for the workload, but we'll validate quality with your evals.

[44:50] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps quickly. Jordan will send runbook, pricing, SOC2 pack. Priya will schedule the deep-dive and share bench checklist. Marcus to set cadence. Alex to share sample traffic and IAM contacts.

[45:30] Alex: We'll aim to get the sample by EOD Friday.

[46:00] Rina: Procurement will review once SOC2 and terms are shared.

[47:20] Priya: Quick question — any org-level constraints we should know? Data residency rules beyond US-EAST?

[47:35] Alex: Not initially, maybe EMEA later. For now keep it US only.

[49:10] Jordan: Any other blockers?

[49:22] Sana: IAM contacts — we will provide two folks. Also need a contact for monitoring integration.

[50:05] Miguel: Also, can Redwood provide sample instrumentation for tracing?

[50:20] Priya: Yes, sample trace spans and SDK snippets. We'll drop them in the shared folder.

[51:45] Marcus: I'll send the calendar invites and a short agenda for next week's deep-dive.

[53:00] Jordan: Great. Final note — we'll keep fallback to hosted off for the pilot unless you explicitly ask to enable it. That should address the egress concern.

[54:12] Alex: Appreciate that.

[55:05] Rina: Quick question about invoices for pilot — tag us as a P.O. will be issued after pilot approval?

[55:30] Jordan: We'll work with procurement — Marcus will follow up.

[56:40] Priya: Ok everyone — thanks, we'll follow up with the materials.
[57:05] Alex: Thanks all.
[57:15] Miguel: Thanks.
[57:30] Marcus: Bye.
